text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today, pulling back from a three-day rally that had pushed the stock to $142.28 on November 13th. The decline follows a modest dip in US crude oil prices to $89.62 per barrel, down from the highs earlier this week. While oil remains elevated and heating oil prices are significantly up from last year (a tailwind for refiners), the stock's retreat suggests profit-taking after the recent three-day gain rather than a fundamental shift in company prospects.

The broader energy complex shows mixed signals: crude prices remain firm, and elevated heating oil demand could support refining margins through winter. However, the stock's 4.3% drop over two weeks indicates investors may be digesting concerns about demand — the holiday shipping slowdown mentioned in recent reports could eventually weigh on fuel consumption, even as near-term heating demand remains strong.
